Independent example replay: use T(q)=1.85−0.05q−0.85q²−0.05q³ and D(q)=0.855−0.045q−0.855q²+0.045q³; solve T′ρ−D′=0 with ρ=(T+sqrt(T²−4D))/2 on q∈[0.2,0.35]. At this level λ>L, the cubic λ²−λT+D has positive constant, linear and cubic coefficients, hence at most two positive roots counting multiplicities; its double root at the stationary point proves this is the unique global maximum in the example.
correctness.rationale: For row-vector occupancy the catastrophe step precedes colonization, yielding the frozen transient product. At zero distance its Perron eigenvalue is 1−r; at infinity the triangular limit gives L=1−r/2. For positive finite distance the off-diagonals are positive, the eigenvalues are distinct, and the smaller eigenvalue is below M₁₁<L. Thus the characteristic polynomial at L has the opposite sign to ρ−L. Direct expansion gives det(LI−M)=(r/4)[rq−c(A−Bq)], so all three comparisons reduce to the level r of q^(k−1)(A−Bq) on 0<q<A/B. For k≤1 this positive function strictly decreases with q from a value above r to zero. For k>1 differentiation puts its sole maximum at q*=(k−1)A/(kB). The maximum H_r(k) strictly decreases with k by comparing at the interior maximizer for the larger k, and its endpoint limits are A>r and 0. Hence the unique critical k, all counts and directions of crossing, tangency and strict inequalities follow. Continuity and the limit at infinity imply finite attainment whenever there is a strict gain, and exclude it in the strict no-gain regime. For k=2 the quadratic threshold and the two example endpoints check. Independently differentiating the larger eigenvalue in q and bisecting near q=0.25654375 gives ρ≈0.957274401341 at d≈1.360456062, consistent with the quoted approximate point up to about 4.4×10⁻⁸ in distance.
residual_risks: The proof's phrase 'compact region 0<q≤A/B' is imprecise; strict comparison at the interior maximizer supplies the needed monotonicity without that wording.
The last digits of the approximate example distance should not be read as exact or as a high-precision certificate.
The classification is of gain over the limiting Perron factor, not uniqueness of the maximizing distance in both strict-gain regimes or a result about mean extinction time.

originality.rationale: The baseline process, exponential kernels and Perron objective belong to Wagner–Ross–Possingham. Their inspected baseline passages calculate the eigenvalue and discuss numerical optima and an apparent plateau. The supported distinct contribution is the exact all-parameter comparison with its infinite-distance limit, including a bounded gain interval, equality at a single interior distance, and no finite maximizer. The closest indexed result concerns a different continuous-time model and compares two finite optima. The bounded comparison is not a claim of historical priority.
residual_risks: Blowes–Connolly full text was not accessible via identified lawful copies. Its qualitative overlap remains material but supplies no evidence of exact coverage.

value.rationale: The exact criterion separates three scenarios that numerical persistence curves can make indistinguishable: an interior strict advantage, an exactly tied finite optimizer, and a limiting benchmark unattained anywhere finite. The natural comparison applies for the entire model parameter domain and explains why a plateau does not prove either a finite optimum or its absence. It is a theoretical diagnostic for this baseline, not a fitted conservation recommendation.
residual_risks: Changing the persistence objective, adding immigration or local extinction, or fitting an empirical dispersal/catastrophe model may change the conclusion.
